# ROOTS-AI™ — C-03 controlled approval register

The nineteen vendor-authored report strings, each with its exact source clause and disposition.
Prepared in response to the ROOTS review of 30 September 2026, section 4.

**Generated by** `npm run evidence:c03-approval`. Each string is quoted from the live content
module, and the set of nineteen is cross-checked against `npm run check:c03` so the two cannot
drift.

## The test ROOTS set

> "Where the wording is a direct participant-facing expression of an existing controlled rule
> and introduces no additional scientific meaning, it may be submitted for final incorporation
> into A1. Where the wording interprets scoring, ranking, protective factors, confidence
> composition, causation, or the meaning of a state beyond what the controlled source actually
> states, it remains a ROOTS content decision."

ROOTS also directed that identifiers and implementation logic are not authority for
participant-facing wording. An identifier proves a string is used; it proves nothing about
whether the wording is supported. No disposition below rests on one.

## Result

| Disposition | Strings | What ROOTS is asked to do |
|---|---|---|
| **ROOTS-issued** | 5 | Confirm provenance. These are not vendor copy. |
| **Submitted for incorporation into A1** | 5 | Approve, amend or reject. |
| **ROOTS content decision** | 9 | Issue the wording, or confirm ours. **Remains proposed until then.** |
| Total | 19 | |

### A correction to our own classification

**5 of the nineteen were written by ROOTS, not by us.** Our wording register classified
them as vendor-drafted because it searched only two sources: the C-03 pack and the issued review
of 24 September. The wording for the Executive Summary driver variants and the three reduced
Triad states was supplied by ROOTS in the direction of **25 September 2026**, which that search
did not cover. ROOTS expressly rejected our earlier proposal ("strongest area(s)") and supplied
replacements under the heading "Approved wording".

We record them here as ROOTS-issued and ask ROOTS to confirm that provenance. We are not
relabelling vendor text as ROOTS text: the direction is quoted, and the decision log entry that
records it predates this review.

## 2. Submitted for incorporation into A1

Each of these is, in our judgement, a direct participant-facing expression of a controlled rule
that adds no scientific meaning. The exact clause relied on is given so ROOTS can test that
judgement rather than accept it.

### `TRIAD_DIAGRAM_LABEL`

> Biological Triad — the elements this view brings together

**Source clause.** C-05 §13 (accessible description of relationship diagrams); report review point 31.

**Why it adds no scientific meaning.** Names the diagram for assistive technology. It states no finding, no value and no relationship — the relationship wording remains the approved TRIAD_NOTE. No scientific meaning is added.

### `WHY.biologicalState`

> This value summarizes the seven-domain scores available in your answers ({available_list}). It is a composite of those domain scores, not a separate measurement.

**Source clause.** C-02 SC-002: *"Mean of available seven domain scores"*, with the available-domain list from the same rule.

**Why it adds no scientific meaning.** Restates SC-002 in participant-facing words: a composite of the listed domain scores, not a separate measurement. It adds no meaning the rule does not already carry.

### `WHY.biologicalStateNull`

> Too few of the seven domains had enough answers for this composite to be produced, so no value is shown.

**Source clause.** C-02 SC-002 null rule: *"Null if fewer than 5 domains available"*, with SC-001 *"null if answered/eligible < 0.50"*.

**Why it adds no scientific meaning.** States the null condition as it is defined. It asserts no cause and no consequence beyond "no value is shown".

### `WHY.opportunity`

> This value is derived from your ROOTS Biological State™ score. It uses no answers beyond those already summarized there.

**Source clause.** C-02 SC-003: *"100 − (Biological State × 0.5)"*.

**Why it adds no scientific meaning.** Says the value is derived from Biological State and uses no further answers. That is exactly what the formula does; the constant itself is not disclosed.

### `WHY.opportunityNull`

> This value is derived from your ROOTS Biological State™ score, which is not available for this assessment.

**Source clause.** C-02 SC-003 null rule: *"Null when Biological State is null"*.

**Why it adds no scientific meaning.** States the null condition as defined.

## 3. ROOTS content decisions

These interpret scoring, ranking, protective factors, confidence composition, causation or the
meaning of a state **beyond what the controlled source states**. They remain proposed vendor
wording and must not become controlled by inference.

We have placed strings here wherever the honest answer was that the source does not support the
wording, including several we would prefer to have accepted. A negative causal claim is still a
claim; a compressed activation rule still carries meaning the rule does not state.

### `CONFIDENCE_COMPOSITE_NOTE`

> The composite Confidence score is produced by the controlled confidence model, which combines these components with fixed weightings. It is not a simple average of the values above.

**Nearest source.** C-02 SC-008 defines the weights (0.50 / 0.30 / 0.20). It supplies no participant-facing wording, and the review of 24 September states the requirement without giving the sentence.

**Why it exceeds that source.** This describes **confidence composition**, which ROOTS names as a reserved category. It also characterises the model ("controlled confidence model", "fixed weightings", "not a simple average") in terms C-02 does not use. We do not treat the existence of SC-008 as authority for how to describe it.

### `WHY.confidence`

> This value comes from three recorded inputs: how much of the questionnaire you answered ({coverage_percent}% of scored questions), the answer confidence you reported yourself ({answer_confidence}/100), and how consistent your responses were within each available domain.

**Nearest source.** C-02 SC-008 names the three inputs. It supplies no participant-facing wording.

**Why it exceeds that source.** **Confidence composition** again, and it goes further than CONFIDENCE_COMPOSITE_NOTE by naming and quantifying the three inputs to the participant. Reserved to ROOTS.

### `WHY.drivers`

> The domains named above were the highest-ranked of the domains that met the eligibility rule in your answers. The domains that met it, in rank order, were: {eligible_list}. Ranking reflects the level of burden reported in those domains; it does not identify a cause.

**Nearest source.** C-02 DRV-001 (eligibility ≥ 25) and DRV-002 (ranking by score descending).

**Why it exceeds that source.** Describes **ranking**, a reserved category, and makes an explicit **causation** statement — *"it does not identify a cause"*. Even a negative causal claim is a claim about meaning. DRV-002 defines how to rank; it does not say how to explain ranking to a participant.

### `WHY.driversNone`

> No domain met the eligibility rule in the available answers, so no driver is ranked. This may reflect missing answers rather than an absence of signals.

**Nearest source.** C-02 DRV-004: *"No domain ≥ 25 → no primary driver"*.

**Why it exceeds that source.** The first clause restates DRV-004. The second — *"This may reflect missing answers rather than an absence of signals"* — is an interpretation of **the meaning of a state**, and is not in the controlled source. We are not willing to submit it as supported.

### `PROTECTIVE_LABELS.P1`

> Regular physical activity

**Nearest source.** C-02 protective factors table, P1: activation rule and value 20. The table defines when the factor is active; it gives no participant-facing name.

**Why it exceeds that source.** **Protective factors** are a reserved category. Naming a factor to a participant is a content decision: our wording compresses an activation rule into a phrase, and the phrase carries meaning the rule does not state.

## What happens to each disposition

| | If ROOTS approves | If ROOTS does not |
|---|---|---|
| ROOTS-issued | Recorded in A1 with its provenance as issued wording | We are wrong about provenance; it moves to section 3 |
| Submitted | Incorporated into A1 as controlled content | Stays proposed, or is replaced with wording ROOTS issues |
| Content decision | Only when ROOTS issues or confirms the wording | **Stays proposed.** The state it covers still renders, with wording marked vendor-authored |

**Nothing here is treated as approved by implementation.** A string being live and tested is not
an argument for approving it, and is not offered as one.

## Cross-check

The nineteen declared here are compared with the vendor-drafted set that `npm run check:c03`
finds independently by searching the controlled sources.

**They match.**
